questions.question: Older trailers do not have spring brakes. What happens if the air supply leaks away?

options.text: The trailer will not have brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer will not have brakes.
questions.explanation: Older trailers do not have spring brakes. If the air supply leaks away, the brakes will not work. The wheels will turn freely without any braking power.

questions.question: If your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks, what should you do?

options.text: Stay in the cab and call for help.
Exit the vehicle and walk away from the tracks.
Signal another driver to push your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Exit the vehicle and walk away from the tracks.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks, leave the vehicle immediately and walk away from the tracks. Call emergency services right away.

questions.question: How can you check that air reaches all trailers before a trip?

options.text: Check for moving air inside each trailer.
Listen for air at the rear shut-off valve.
Feel for air at the front shut-off valve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Listen for air at the rear shut-off valve.
questions.explanation: To check that air reaches all trailers, open the shut-off valves at the rear of the last trailer. Listen for air escaping. If you hear air, the system is supplying air to the entire vehicle.

questions.question: How should you apply brakes on a vehicle with an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS)?

options.text: The same way as a vehicle without ABS.
While placing the vehicle in neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same way as a vehicle without ABS.
questions.explanation: Brake a vehicle with ABS the same way you would brake a vehicle without ABS.

questions.question: What happens when the wheels of a trailer lock up?

options.text: The vehicle will keep steering control.

questions.explanation: When a trailer's wheels lock up, the trailer may swing out and hit other vehicles. This is more likely to happen with lightly-loaded trailers.

questions.question: Operating combination vehicles requires ____ operating single vehicles.

options.text: About the same level of skill as

questions.explanation: Combination vehicles are heavier and longer than single vehicles. They require more driving skill to operate safely.

questions.question: What color identifies emergency or supply lines on air brake systems?
questions.explanation: Air lines are sometimes color-coded. Blue is used for service lines and red is used for emergency lines. This helps drivers avoid mistakes when connecting air lines.

questions.question: During a trip, the ____ should be open.
questions.explanation: When starting a trip, open all shut-off valves except the last ones on the rear trailer. This ensures air reaches the brakes on all trailers and does not escape from the back of the vehicle.

questions.question: If a trailer begins to skid, what should the driver do?

options.text: Turn the steering wheel quickly left and right.

questions.explanation: If your trailer skids, release the brakes. The wheels will grip the road again and the trailer will straighten out.

questions.question: When crossing traffic in a combination vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Assume other drivers will make room for your vehicle.
Wait for a gap large enough for your vehicle to safely cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for a gap large enough for your vehicle to safely cross.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles need more road space than other vehicles. When crossing traffic, wait for a large enough gap to safely cross.

questions.question: If a parked trailer does not have spring brakes, how should you keep it from moving?

options.text: Park it against a wall or another vehicle.
Park it on a slight incline.

questions.explanation: If a parked trailer does not have spring brakes, use wheel chocks to prevent it from moving.

questions.question: When should you look into the back of the fifth wheel?

options.text: If your vehicle begins to skid.

questions.explanation: When inspecting a coupling, look under the trailer and into the back of the fifth wheel. Make sure the fifth wheel jaws are locked around the kingpin shank.

questions.question: After you connect the air lines to the trailer during coupling, what should you do next?
questions.explanation: After connecting the air lines to the trailer during coupling, supply air to the trailer. Following the correct coupling steps is important for safe operation.

questions.question: What is the Johnson bar?

options.text: A hand valve that operates the trailer brakes.
A valve that shows the fuel level.
A valve that limits the amount of cargo.

questions.correctAnswerText: A hand valve that operates the trailer brakes.
questions.explanation: The trailer hand valve is also called the trolley valve or Johnson bar. It operates the trailer brakes and should only be used to test them. Using it while driving can cause a skid.

questions.question: What does the emergency air line supply air to?
questions.explanation: The emergency air line (also called the supply line) has two jobs. It supplies air to the trailer air tanks and controls the emergency brakes on combination vehicles.

questions.question: When should the trailer hand valve be used?

options.text: To check the connection between the trailer and tractor.

questions.explanation: The trailer hand valve (also called the trolley valve or Johnson bar) operates the trailer brakes. Use it only when testing brakes. Using it while driving can cause a skid.

questions.question: Should the trailer hand valve be used for parking?

options.text: Yes, always use it for parking.
Only use it for parking on a downgrade.
No, never use it for parking.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, never use it for parking.
questions.explanation: Never use the trailer hand valve for parking. Using it may release air pressure from the braking system and release the brakes holding the vehicle. Use the parking brake or wheel chocks instead.

questions.question: Trailers built before which year are not required to have spring brakes?
questions.explanation: Trailers built before 1975 are not required to have spring brakes. When parking a trailer without spring brakes, use wheel chocks to prevent it from rolling.

questions.question: In a vehicle with an automatic tractor protection valve, the valve will pop out when air pressure drops to what level?
questions.explanation: In vehicles with an automatic tractor protection valve, the valve pops out if air pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi. When the valve pops out, it closes and stops the flow of air.

questions.question: Why should you not use the trailer hand valve while driving?

options.text: It will disconnect from the vehicle.
You will stop the vehicle too quickly.

questions.explanation: Never use the trailer hand valve while driving. Using it while driving can cause your trailer to skid.
